question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who always expects the worst possible outcome in any situation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pessimist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Pessimist" means a person who always expects the worst possible outcome and dwells on the negative aspects of a situation, from the Latin “pessimus” (worst), the superlative of “malus” (bad). (निराशावादी व्यक्ति)
◦ Example: Being a pessimist, he was convinced the project would fail even before it began.

 

• The suffix "-ist" often denotes a believer in or follower of a particular doctrine or attitude, as in “Optimist,” “Fatalist,” and “Realist.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Optimist (आशावादी): A person who is hopeful and expects the best possible outcome, from Latin “optimus” (best).

 

• Option 3: Fatalist (भाग्यवादी): A person who believes that all events are predetermined by fate and cannot be changed.

 

• Option 4: Cynic (संशयवादी): A person who distrusts the sincerity or goodness of human motives and intentions.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Pessimist" frequently asked in SSC: Optimist (expects the best — antonym), Fatalist (believes in predetermined fate), Cynic (distrusts human motives), Defeatist (readily accepts defeat) and Misanthrope (hates mankind).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys property

2. Workaholic (काम में डूबा रहने वाला): A person compulsively addicted to work

3. Xenophile (विदेशी संस्कृति प्रेमी): A person strongly attracted to foreign cultures

4. Yokel (देहाती व्यक्ति): An unsophisticated person from the countryside

5. Amateur (अव्यवसायी): A person who does something without formal training or pay

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Lasting for a very short time; short-lived or transitory.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Ephemeral.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Ephemeral" means lasting for a very short time; short-lived or transitory, from the Greek “epi-” (on) and “hemera” (day) — literally “lasting only a day.” (क्षणभंगुर)
◦ Example: Fame in the world of viral videos is often ephemeral, fading within days.

 

• The Greek root "hemera" means day, giving words like “Ephemeral” (lasting a day) — contrast it with roots like “aeternus” (eternity), seen in long-duration words such as “Eternal” and “Perpetual.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Perennial (बारहमासी): Lasting or existing for a long time, or recurring repeatedly; often used of plants that live for several years.

 

• Option 2: Eternal (शाश्वत): Lasting forever; without beginning or end.

 

• Option 4: Perpetual (निरंतर): Continuing indefinitely without interruption or end.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Ephemeral" frequently asked in SSC: Transient (passing quickly), Fleeting (lasting only a moment), Momentary (very brief), Evanescent (soon disappearing) and Transitory (not permanent).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Bigot (कट्टरपंथी): A person intolerant of differing opinions or beliefs

2. Charlatan (ढोंगी): A person falsely claiming special knowledge or skill

3. Dilettante (अल्पज्ञ शौकिया): A person with a superficial interest in an art

4. Epicure (स्वादिष्ट भोजन का शौकीन): A person devoted to refined, especially culinary, pleasure

5. Fugitive (फरार अपराधी): A person fleeing from custody or in hiding

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Government by a single ruler who holds absolute, unlimited power.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Autocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Autocracy" means a system of government in which one person holds absolute, unrestricted power, from the Greek “autos” (self) and “kratos” (power/rule). (निरंकुश शासन)
◦ Example: Under the czar's autocracy, no law could be passed without his personal approval.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes rule or government, and the first part of the word tells us who holds the power.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Democracy (लोकतंत्र): Government by the people, typically exercised through elected representatives, from Greek “demos” (people).

 

• Option 2: Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): Government by a small privileged ruling class, especially the hereditary nobility, from Greek “aristos” (best).

 

• Option 3: Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government by religious leaders claiming divine sanction, from Greek “theos” (god).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Democracy (rule by the people), Aristocracy (rule by the nobility), Theocracy (rule by religious authority), Bureaucracy (rule by officials), Plutocracy (rule by the wealthy) and Meritocracy (rule by the most talented).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Herald (अग्रदूत): A person or sign announcing the approach of something

2. Interloper (अनधिकार प्रवेशी): A person who interferes in matters without invitation

3. Juggernaut (विशाल अजेय शक्ति): A huge, unstoppable force that crushes everything ahead

4. Kleptomaniac (चोरी का उन्माद रखने वाला): A person with an irresistible compulsion to steal

5. Luminary (विख्यात व्यक्ति): A person who is an inspiring leader in a field

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes that people are motivated purely by self-interest and doubts the sincerity of others' intentions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Cynic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cynic" means a person who doubts the sincerity of others' motives and believes people act out of self-interest, from the Greek “kynikos” (dog-like), a name given to the ancient philosophical school whose followers scorned social conventions. (निंदक)
◦ Example: Years of being cheated turned him into a cynic who trusted no one's intentions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Skeptic (संशयवादी): One who habitually doubts accepted beliefs or claims, especially those not backed by evidence.

 

• Option 3: Pessimist (निराशावादी): One who always expects the worst possible outcome in any situation.

 

• Option 4: Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): One who hates or distrusts mankind in general, avoiding human society.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Cynic" frequently asked in SSC: Skeptic (one who doubts accepted beliefs or claims), Pessimist (one who always expects the worst), Misanthrope (one who hates mankind), Stoic (one who remains indifferent to pleasure and pain), Nihilist (one who rejects all religious and moral principles), and Fatalist (one who believes events are predetermined by fate).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philanthropist (परोपकारी): A person who works for the welfare of others

2. Bibliophile (पुस्तक-प्रेमी): A lover or collector of books

3. Sybarite (भोग-विलासी): A person fond of luxury and pleasure

4. Epicure (खाने-पीने का शौकीन): A person who takes particular pleasure in fine food and drink

5. Zenith (चरम बिंदु): The highest point or peak of something

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

Spoken or performed without any prior preparation or rehearsal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Extempore.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Extempore" means spoken or done without any prior preparation or notes, from the Latin “ex tempore” (out of the time, i.e., on the spur of the moment). (बिना तैयारी के)
◦ Example: She delivered a brilliant extempore speech on the topic given to her only five minutes earlier.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Verbatim (शब्दशः): Repeated or copied in exactly the same words, word for word, from Latin “verbum” (word).

 

• Option 3: Monologue (एकालाप): A long speech delivered by one person alone, especially in a play, from Greek “monos” (single) and “logos” (speech).

 

• Option 4: Rhetoric (वाक्पटुता): The art of effective or persuasive speaking or writing, from Greek “rhetorike” (oratory).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Extempore" frequently asked in SSC: Impromptu (done without preparation, on the spur of the moment), Ad-lib (to speak or perform without preparation), Spontaneous (happening naturally without planning), Verbose (using more words than needed), and Fluent (able to speak smoothly and easily).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A person with no fixed home who moves from place to place

2. Hermit (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in solitude, often for religious reasons

3. Panacea (रामबाण / सर्वरोगनाशक): A remedy or solution for all difficulties or diseases

4. Placebo (मिथ्या औषधि): A substance with no therapeutic effect given to satisfy a patient

5. Cliché (घिसी-पिटी बात): A phrase or opinion overused to the point of losing original meaning

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The art of using language effectively and persuasively in speaking or writing.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rhetoric.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Rhetoric" means the art of using language effectively and persuasively in speaking or writing, from the Greek “rhetorike” (the art of an orator). (वाक्पटुता)
◦ Example: The politician's rhetoric moved the crowd, even though his promises were vague.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Eloquence (प्रवाहपूर्ण वाणी): The quality of being fluent and persuasive in speech or writing, from Latin “eloqui” (to speak out).

 

• Option 2: Diction (शब्द-चयन): The choice and use of words, or a speaker's manner of enunciation, from Latin “dictio” (a saying).

 

• Option 4: Semantics (अर्थविज्ञान): The branch of linguistics dealing with the meaning of words and sentences, from Greek “semantikos” (significant).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Rhetoric" frequently asked in SSC: Eloquence (fluent and persuasive speech), Oratory (the art of public speaking), Diction (choice of words), Elocution (the skill of clear and expressive speech), and Verbosity (the use of more words than needed).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Ascetic (तपस्वी): One who practises severe self-discipline and abstains from pleasure

2. Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person who is fanatically committed to a cause

3. Bigot (कट्टरपंथी): A person intolerant of opinions different from their own

4. Connoisseur (पारखी): An expert judge in matters of art or taste

5. Vagabond (आवारा): A person who wanders from place to place without a home

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who attacks or criticises cherished beliefs, traditions, or established institutions.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Iconoclast.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Iconoclast" means a person who attacks or criticises cherished beliefs, traditions, or established institutions, from the Greek “eikon” (image) and “klastes” (breaker), originally referring to one who destroys religious images. (परंपराओं का विरोधी)
◦ Example: As an iconoclast, she constantly challenged the university's outdated traditions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Zealot (कट्टर समर्थक): A person who is fanatically committed to a cause or belief, from Greek “zelos” (zeal).

 

• Option 2: Conformist (अनुरूपतावादी): A person who readily follows accepted beliefs, customs, or practices without question.

 

• Option 3: Loyalist (निष्ठावान): A person who remains faithful and loyal to an established authority, government, or institution.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Iconoclast" frequently asked in SSC: Rebel (one who resists authority or convention), Dissident (one who openly opposes official policy), Heretic (one who holds beliefs contrary to established doctrine), Nonconformist (one who does not conform to accepted beliefs), and Radical (one who favours extreme change).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Philatelist (डाक-टिकट संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects postage stamps

2. Numismatist (सिक्का संग्रहकर्ता): A person who collects or studies coins

3. Misogynist (स्त्री-द्वेषी): A person who dislikes or is prejudiced against women

4. Cartographer (मानचित्रकार): A person who draws or makes maps

5. Nostalgia (विगत काल की याद): A sentimental longing for the past

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

An abnormal or irrational fear of confined or enclosed spaces.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Claustrophobia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Claustrophobia" means an abnormal or irrational fear of confined or enclosed spaces, from the Latin “claustrum” (a closed place) and the Greek “phobos” (fear). (बंद जगहों का भय)
◦ Example: He refused to take the elevator because of his severe claustrophobia.

 

• The suffix "-phobia" always denotes an abnormal or irrational fear, and the first part of the word tells us what is feared.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Agoraphobia (भीड़ या खुले स्थानों का भय): An abnormal fear of open spaces or crowded public places, from Greek “agora” (marketplace).

 

• Option 3: Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): An abnormal fear of heights, from Greek “akros” (topmost, peak).

 

• Option 4: Hydrophobia (जल का भय): An abnormal fear of water, from Greek “hydor” (water).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phobia" words frequently asked in SSC: Agoraphobia (open or crowded spaces), Acrophobia (heights), Hydrophobia (water), Xenophobia (foreigners or strangers), Arachnophobia (spiders), Nyctophobia (darkness), and Photophobia (light).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Zoologist (प्राणीशास्त्री): A person who studies animals

2. Entomologist (कीट-विज्ञानी): A person who studies insects

3. Ornithologist (पक्षी-विज्ञानी): A person who studies birds

4. Plutocracy (धनिकतंत्र): Government by the wealthy

5. Theocracy (धर्मतंत्र): Government by religious leaders in the name of God

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A place where coins are officially manufactured by the government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mint.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mint" means a place where coins are officially manufactured by the government, from the Latin “moneta” (coinage), the surname of the Roman goddess Juno in whose temple coins were struck. (जहाँ सिक्के बनाये जाते है)
◦ Example: The Royal Mint has produced coins for the United Kingdom for over a thousand years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Foundry (ढलाई-घर): A workshop or factory where metal is cast into shape, from Old French “fondre” (to melt).

 

• Option 3: Treasury (राजकोष): A place where public or government funds and valuables are kept and managed.

 

• Option 4: Arsenal (शस्त्रागार): A place where weapons, ammunition, and military equipment are made or stored.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Mint" frequently asked in SSC: Foundry (where metal is cast), Treasury (where public funds are kept), Arsenal (where weapons are stored), Granary (where grain is stored), and Armoury (a store of weapons).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives in seclusion, avoiding others

2. Interpreter (दुभाषिया): A person who translates speech orally from one language to another

3. Polyglot (बहुभाषाविद): A person who knows and can use several languages

4. Utopia (काल्पनिक आदर्श समाज): An imagined place or state in which everything is perfect

5. Amnesty (क्षमादान): An official pardon for people convicted of political offences

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is scornfully indifferent to accepted moral and social values, doubting the existence of any genuine goodness or virtue.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cynic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cynic" means a person who is scornfully indifferent to accepted moral and social values and doubts the existence of genuine goodness, from the Greek “kynikos” (dog-like), the name given to the ancient philosophical sect that rejected conventional norms. (निंदक / आलोचक)
◦ Example: As a hardened cynic, he mocked every act of charity as mere self-promotion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Nihilist (शून्यवादी): One who rejects all religious and moral principles, often believing that life is without objective meaning.

 

• Option 2: Stoic (स्थितप्रज्ञ): One who remains indifferent to both pleasure and pain, enduring hardship without complaint, from the Greek “stoa” (porch, where the philosopher Zeno taught).

 

• Option 4: Hedonist (सुखवादी): One who believes that the pursuit of pleasure and self-indulgence is the most important goal in life, from Greek “hedone” (pleasure).

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Cynic" frequently asked in SSC: Nihilist (one who rejects all moral principles), Stoic (one indifferent to pleasure and pain), Hedonist (one who lives for pleasure), Misanthrope (one who hates mankind), and Skeptic (one who doubts accepted beliefs).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Panegyric (प्रशस्ति भाषण): A public speech or published text in praise of someone

2. Diatribe (कटु आलोचना): A forceful and bitter verbal attack against someone

3. Plebiscite (जनमत संग्रह): A direct vote by the electorate on an important public question

4. Vandal (विध्वंसक): A person who deliberately destroys or damages property

5. Mercenary (भाड़े का सैनिक): A soldier hired to serve in a foreign army for payment

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who eats the flesh of other human beings.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cannibal.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Cannibal" means a person who eats the flesh of other human beings, from the Spanish “Canibal”, a variant of “Caribal”, referring to the Carib people of the West Indies who were believed to practise this. (नरभक्षी)
◦ Example: The isolated tribe was, according to old explorers' accounts, said to be cannibal in its rituals.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Carnivore (मांसाहारी): An animal that feeds on the flesh of other animals, from Latin “caro” (flesh) and “vorare” (to devour).

 

• Option 2: Vegetarian (शाकाहारी): A person who does not eat meat or fish.

 

• Option 3: Scavenger (अवशेषभक्षी): An animal, or a person, that feeds on dead or decaying organic matter, or collects discarded items.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Cannibal" frequently asked in SSC: Carnivore (an animal that eats flesh), Herbivore (an animal that eats plants), Omnivore (one that eats both plants and flesh), Scavenger (one that feeds on refuse or carrion), and Predator (an animal that hunts other animals for food).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Fugitive (फरार व्यक्ति): A person who has escaped from captivity or is in hiding

2. Deportee (निर्वासित व्यक्ति): A person expelled from a country by official order

3. Autocracy (एकतंत्र): Government by one person with absolute power

4. Chronicle (इतिवृत्त): A factual written account of events in the order they occurred

5. Saga (वीरगाथा): A long story of heroic achievement or adventure

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The scientific study of human beings, their origins, societies, and cultures.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Anthropology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anthropology" means the scientific study of human beings, their origins, societies, and cultures, from the Greek “anthropos” (human being) and “logos” (study). (मानवशास्त्र)
◦ Example: She is pursuing a degree in anthropology to understand how different cultures have evolved.

 

• The suffix "-logy" always denotes the study of something, and the first part of the word tells us what subject is being studied.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Archaeology (पुरातत्वशास्त्र): The study of human history through the excavation of ancient sites and the analysis of artefacts, from Greek “arkhaios” (ancient).

 

• Option 3: Ethnology (नृजातिविज्ञान): The branch of study that compares and analyses the characteristics of different peoples and cultures, from Greek “ethnos” (nation, people).

 

• Option 4: Sociology (समाजशास्त्र): The study of the development, structure, and functioning of human society, from Latin “socius” (companion) and Greek “logos” (study).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-logy" words frequently asked in SSC: Archaeology (ancient human history and artefacts), Sociology (human society), Etymology (origin of words), Entomology (insects), Ornithology (birds), Cardiology (the heart), and Genealogy (family descent).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Elegy (शोकगीत): A poem of serious reflection, typically mourning the dead

2. Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): Words inscribed on a tombstone in memory of the deceased

3. Requiem (मृतकों के लिए प्रार्थना गीत): A piece of music or service for the repose of the dead

4. Homily (उपदेश): A talk on a religious or moral topic, often tediously moralistic

5. Aphorism (सूक्ति): A concise statement expressing a general truth or principle

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A formal speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially one delivered in honour of a person who has died.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Eulogy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Eulogy" means a formal speech or piece of writing that praises someone highly, especially one delivered in honour of a person who has died, from the Greek “eu” (well) and “logos” (speech/word). (प्रशस्ति / गुणगान)
◦ Example: His closest friend delivered a moving eulogy at the funeral.

 

• The prefix "eu-" always denotes good or well, as seen in words like euphony (a pleasant sound) and euphemism (a mild expression for something harsh).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Elegy (शोकगीत): A mournful poem or song, typically a lament for the dead, from Greek “elegos” (a lament).

 

• Option 3: Panegyric (प्रशस्ति भाषण): A formal public speech or written text praising a person, achievement, or thing, not necessarily connected with death.

 

• Option 4: Epitaph (समाधि-लेख): Words inscribed on a tombstone or monument in memory of the person buried there.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Eulogy" frequently asked in SSC: Elegy (a mournful poem for the dead), Panegyric (formal praise of a person or thing), Epitaph (words inscribed on a tomb), Obituary (a published notice of death with a short biography), and Requiem (a service or music for the dead).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Xenophobe (विदेशी-द्वेषी): A person who has an intense dislike or fear of foreigners

2. Anglophile (अंग्रेज-प्रेमी): A person who greatly admires England and English customs

3. Workaholic (कार्य-व्यसनी): A person who is addicted to working excessively hard

4. Kleptomaniac (चोरी की सनक वाला): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

5. Megalomaniac (महत्वाकांक्षा-ग्रस्त): A person obsessed with their own power or importance

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A written account of a person's life composed by that person himself or herself.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Autobiography.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Autobiography" means a written account of a person's own life, composed by that person, from the Greek “autos” (self), “bios” (life) and “graphein” (to write). (आत्मकथा)
◦ Example: Gandhi's autobiography, "The Story of My Experiments with Truth", remains widely read.

 

• The suffix "-graphy" always denotes writing or a written record of something, and combined with "auto-" (self) it specifically means writing about oneself.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Biography (जीवनी): A written account of another person's life, from Greek “bios” (life) and “graphein” (to write).

 

• Option 2: Memoir (संस्मरण): A written account focusing on the author's personal experiences, observations, or a particular period, rather than the whole life.

 

• Option 4: Chronicle (इतिवृत्त): A factual written record of events, arranged in the order in which they occurred, without personal interpretation.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-graphy" words frequently asked in SSC: Biography (an account of another's life), Bibliography (a list of books on a subject), Choreography (the composing of dance movements), Calligraphy (the art of beautiful handwriting), Cartography (the making of maps), and Geography (the study of the earth's physical features).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभा वाला व्यक्ति): A young person with exceptional talent or ability

2. Novice (नौसिखिया): A person new to or inexperienced in a field or activity

3. Virtuoso (निपुण कलाकार): A person highly skilled in a particular art, especially music

4. Maestro (उस्ताद): A distinguished figure in a particular field, especially music

5. Refugee (शरणार्थी): A person forced to leave their country to escape war, persecution, or disaster

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who believes in the abolition of all government and law, and vehemently opposes any form of authority, control, or tradition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Anarchist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Anarchist" means a person who believes in the abolition of all government and law, and vehemently opposes any authority, control, or tradition, from the Greek “an-” (without) and “arkhos” (ruler/leader). (अराजकतावादी)
◦ Example: The anarchist pamphlets called for the complete dismantling of the state.

 

• The suffix "-ist" often denotes a believer in or follower of a particular doctrine or practice, as in socialist, capitalist, and anarchist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Autocrat (एकतंत्री शासक): A ruler who holds absolute and unrestricted power, from Greek “autos” (self) and “kratos” (power/rule).

 

• Option 2: Loyalist (निष्ठावान): A person who remains steadfastly faithful to an established government or authority.

 

• Option 3: Bureaucrat (नौकरशाह): An official in a government department, often one who rigidly follows established rules and procedures.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Anarchist" frequently asked in SSC: Rebel (one who resists authority), Iconoclast (one who attacks cherished traditions), Dissident (one who openly opposes official policy), Insurgent (one who rises in revolt against authority), and Nihilist (one who rejects all governing principles).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): Government by a small privileged ruling class

2. Oligarchy (अल्पतंत्र): Government by a small group of powerful people

3. Referendum (जनमत संग्रह): A general vote by the electorate on a single political question

4. Franchise (मताधिकार): The right to vote in public elections

5. Insurgent (विद्रोही): A person fighting against an established government or authority

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

No longer in use or practice; outdated and replaced by something newer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Obsolete.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obsolete" means no longer in use or practice, having been replaced by something newer, from the Latin “obsolescere” (to fall into disuse). (अप्रचलित)
◦ Example: Floppy disks have become obsolete since the arrival of cloud storage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Archaic (पुरातन): Very old-fashioned or characteristic of an earlier, often ancient, period, especially in language or style, from Greek “arkhaios” (ancient).

 

• Option 3: Antique (प्राचीन वस्तु): An object belonging to or dating from an earlier period, valued for its age and craftsmanship.

 

• Option 4: Vintage (उत्कृष्ट पुराना): Denoting something of high quality from the past, especially wine of a particular year or classic old items.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Obsolete" frequently asked in SSC: Archaic (very old-fashioned, especially in language), Antique (a valuable old object), Redundant (no longer needed), Outmoded (no longer fashionable or acceptable), and Defunct (no longer existing or functioning).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Adage (कहावत): A short, traditional saying expressing a general truth

2. Vagrant (आवारा): A person without a settled home or regular work who wanders

3. Laureate (सम्मानित विद्वान / कवि): A person honoured for outstanding creative or intellectual achievement

4. Suffrage (मताधिकार): The right to vote in political elections

5. Amnesia (स्मृतिलोप): A partial or total loss of memory

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who is highly skilled in an art, especially in playing music.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Virtuoso.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Virtuoso" means a person highly skilled in an art, especially music, from the Italian “virtuoso”, ultimately from the Latin “virtus” (excellence, skill). (कुशल कलाकार)
◦ Example: The young pianist performed like a true virtuoso.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Prodigy (अद्भुत प्रतिभाशाली व्यक्ति): A young person, especially a child, with exceptional natural talent.

 

• Option 3: Maestro (उस्ताद संगीतकार): A distinguished conductor or teacher of music, especially classical music.

 

• Option 4: Novice (नौसिखिया): A person who is new to and inexperienced in a field or activity.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Virtuoso" frequently asked in SSC: Maestro (a distinguished conductor or performer of music), Prodigy (a young person with exceptional talent), Connoisseur (an expert judge in matters of taste), Savant (a person of great learning), Adept (someone highly skilled at something) and Doyen (the most respected/senior person in a field).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Misanthrope (मानवद्वेषी): One who hates or distrusts mankind

2. Philanthropist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person who donates generously to help others

3. Xenophobia (विदेशियों से घृणा या भय): Intense dislike or fear of foreigners

4. Claustrophobia (बंद स्थानों का भय): Extreme fear of confined or enclosed spaces

5. Acrophobia (ऊंचाई का भय): Extreme fear of heights

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who loves and collects books.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Bibliophile.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Bibliophile" means a person who loves and collects books, from the Greek “biblion” (book) and “philos” (loving). (पुस्तक-प्रेमी)
◦ Example: As a bibliophile, she spent every weekend browsing old bookshops.

 

• The suffix "-phile" always denotes a love or strong liking for something, and the first part of the word tells us what is loved.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Bibliomaniac (पुस्तक-संग्रह का उन्मादी): A person with an excessive, obsessive passion for collecting books.

 

• Option 2: Bibliophobe (पुस्तक-भीरु): A person who fears or dislikes books.

 

• Option 4: Bibliopole (पुस्तक विक्रेता): A person who buys and sells books, especially rare ones.

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-phile" words frequently asked in SSC: Anglophile (English culture and people), Francophile (France and its culture), Xenophile (foreigners or foreign things), Audiophile (high-quality sound reproduction), Cinephile (films) and Technophile (technology).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Somnambulist (निद्रा में चलने वाला व्यक्ति): A person who walks while asleep

2. Nostalgia (विगत काल की मधुर याद): A sentimental longing for the past

3. Ambidextrous (दोनों हाथों से समान दक्ष): Able to use both hands equally well

4. Vegetarian (शाकाहारी व्यक्ति): A person who does not eat meat

5. Carnivorous (मांसाहारी): Feeding on the flesh of other animals

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A temporary or permanent decrease in the severity of a disease, or a reduction in a penalty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Remission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Remission" means a temporary or permanent lessening of the severity of a disease, or a reduction of a penalty, from the Latin “remittere” (to send back, slacken). (रोग निवृत्ति / दंड में कमी)
◦ Example: The doctors were relieved to see the cancer go into remission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Reprieve (दंड-स्थगन): A temporary postponement or cancellation of a punishment, especially execution.

 

• Option 2: Amnesty (सामान्य क्षमादान): An official pardon granted, especially for political offences, to a group of people.

 

• Option 3: Absolution (पापमुक्ति / क्षमा): Formal release from guilt or penalty, especially in a religious sense.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Remission" frequently asked in SSC: Reprieve (postponement of punishment), Amnesty (a general pardon), Absolution (formal forgiveness of sin), Pardon (official forgiveness for a crime), Abatement (a reduction in intensity or amount) and Convalescence (gradual recovery of health after illness).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Herbivorous (शाकाहारी (प्राणी)): Feeding only on plants

2. Omnivorous (सर्वाहारी): Eating both plant and animal food

3. Ambivert (उभयमुखी व्यक्ति): A person with both introvert and extrovert traits

4. Recluse (एकांतवासी): A person who lives alone, avoiding others

5. Vagabond (आवारा व्यक्ति): A person who wanders with no fixed home

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

The use of deception or trickery, especially in legal or political matters, to achieve one's purpose.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Chicanery.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Chicanery" means the use of deceptive, trickery-based methods to achieve one's purpose. (छल-कपट)
◦ Example: The lawyer was accused of using chicanery to win the case.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Subterfuge (छद्म उपाय): A deceptive strategy or trick used to avoid blame or achieve an end.

 

• Option 3: Duplicity (द्वि-आचरण): Deceitfulness in speech or behaviour, especially by saying different things to different people.

 

• Option 4: Sophistry (कुतर्क): The use of clever but false arguments, especially with the intention to deceive.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Chicanery" frequently asked in SSC: Subterfuge (a deceptive trick or strategy), Duplicity (deceitfulness in speech or conduct), Sophistry (clever but false reasoning), Guile (sly or cunning intelligence), Deception (the act of deceiving) and Skulduggery (underhand or unscrupulous behaviour).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Nomad (खानाबदोश): A member of a people with no fixed home

2. Hermit (सन्यासी): A person living in solitude, often for religious reasons

3. Iconoclast (परंपरा-भंजक): One who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions

4. Zealot (कट्टर अनुयायी): A person fanatically devoted to a cause

5. Chauvinist (अंध-पक्षपाती व्यक्ति): One showing excessive, biased loyalty to their own group

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A system of government in which priests or religious leaders rule in the name of God or a deity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Theocracy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Theocracy" means a system of government ruled by religious leaders in the name of a deity, from the Greek “theos” (god) and “kratos” (rule, power). (धर्मशासन)
◦ Example: Ancient Tibet was, for centuries, governed as a theocracy.

 

• The suffix "-cracy" always denotes rule or government by, and the first part of the word tells us who or what governs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Autocracy (एकतंत्र): Government by a single person having unlimited power, from the Greek “autos” (self).

 

• Option 3: Aristocracy (कुलीनतंत्र): Government by a small privileged class, especially the hereditary nobility.

 

• Option 4: Plutocracy (धनिकतंत्र): Government by the wealthy, from the Greek “ploutos” (wealth).

 

NOTE

 

• Other "-cracy" words frequently asked in SSC: Autocracy (one ruler with absolute power), Aristocracy (a hereditary nobility), Plutocracy (the wealthy), Bureaucracy (government officials/departments), Democracy (the people) and Meritocracy (those with merit).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Loquacious (बातूनी): Tending to talk a great deal

2. Taciturn (मितभाषी): Reserved and saying very little

3. Garrulous (बकबकिया): Excessively talkative, especially about trivial matters

4. Gregarious (मिलनसार): Fond of company; sociable

5. Introvert (अंतर्मुखी व्यक्ति): A shy, reserved person who prefers solitude

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A harmless substance or treatment given to a patient for its psychological benefit rather than any physiological effect.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Placebo.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Placebo" means a harmless substance given to a patient for its psychological rather than medicinal benefit, from the Latin “placebo” (I shall please). (धोखे की दवा)
◦ Example: Half the patients in the trial were given a placebo instead of the actual medicine.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Panacea (रामबाण औषधि): A solution or remedy claimed to cure all problems or diseases.

 

• Option 2: Antidote (प्रतिविष): A medicine taken to counteract a particular poison.

 

• Option 4: Prophylactic (रोग-निवारक औषधि): A medicine or action used to prevent disease.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Placebo" frequently asked in SSC: Panacea (a cure-all remedy), Antidote (a substance that counteracts poison), Prophylactic (a preventive medicine or measure), Sedative (a drug that calms or induces sleep) and Tonic (a medicine taken to give a feeling of vigour).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Extrovert (बहिर्मुखी व्यक्ति): An outgoing, socially confident person

2. Amnesiac (स्मृतिलोप-पीड़ित व्यक्ति): A person suffering from loss of memory

3. Insomniac (अनिद्रा-रोगी): A person unable to sleep normally

4. Hypochondriac (काल्पनिक रोगों से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person abnormally anxious about their health

5. Kleptomaniac (चोरी की धुन से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person with an uncontrollable urge to steal

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A place where a collection of wild or unusual animals is kept, especially for exhibition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Menagerie.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Menagerie" means a place where a collection of wild or exotic animals is kept, especially for exhibition, from the French “ménagerie”, related to “ménage” (household). (पशु संग्रहालय)
◦ Example: The old palace once housed a royal menagerie of lions and peacocks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Aviary (पक्षीशाला): A large enclosure for keeping birds.

 

• Option 2: Apiary (मधुमक्खी पालन गृह): A place, typically with a number of hives, where bees are kept.

 

• Option 3: Sanctuary (अभयारण्य): A protected area of refuge for wildlife, especially threatened species.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Menagerie" frequently asked in SSC: Aviary (a place for keeping birds), Apiary (a place for keeping bees), Vivarium (an enclosure for keeping animals under natural conditions), Aquarium (a place for keeping fish) and Sanctuary (a protected refuge for wildlife).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Pyromaniac (आगजनी की धुन से ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person obsessively driven to set fires

2. Megalomaniac (महत्वोन्माद-ग्रस्त व्यक्ति): A person with an obsessive desire for power

3. Egoist (अहंवादी): A person excessively concerned with self-interest

4. Altruist (परोपकारी व्यक्ति): A person unselfishly concerned for others' welfare

5. Agnostic (अज्ञेयवादी): One who believes God's existence cannot be known

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A building or room in which dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mortuary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Mortuary" means a building or room where dead bodies are kept before burial or cremation, from the Latin “mortuus” (dead). (शवगृह)
◦ Example: The body was taken to the hospital mortuary for a post-mortem examination.

 

• The root "mort-" (from Latin “mors”, death) always relates to death, as seen in words like mortal, mortician, and immortal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Crematorium (शवदाहगृह): A place where dead bodies are cremated.

 

• Option 3: Cemetery (कब्रिस्तान): A large burial ground, especially one not attached to a church.

 

• Option 4: Sepulchre (समाधि): A small room or monument used as a burial place.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words built on the root "mort-" (death) frequently asked in SSC: Mortal (subject to death), Immortal (living forever), Mortician (a person who prepares the dead for burial), Post-mortem (an examination after death) and Moribund (at the point of death).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Atheist (नास्तिक): One who does not believe in God's existence

2. Puritan (अति-नैतिकतावादी व्यक्ति): A person with very strict moral or religious views

3. Renegade (धर्मत्यागी / विद्रोही): One who deserts and betrays a cause or group

4. Turncoat (दल-बदलू): A person who switches loyalty for personal gain

5. Martinet (कठोर अनुशासक): A very strict disciplinarian

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Impostor.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Impostor" means a person who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive others, from the Latin “imponere” (to impose upon). (धोखेबाज)
◦ Example: The police soon discovered that the visiting officer was an impostor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Impersonator (नकलची): A person who imitates or copies the behaviour or appearance of another, often for entertainment.

 

• Option 3: Charlatan (ढोंगी): A person falsely claiming to have special knowledge or skill.

 

• Option 4: Sycophant (चापलूस): A person who flatters someone to gain personal advantage.

 

NOTE

 

• Other words close in meaning to "Impostor" frequently asked in SSC: Impersonator (one who imitates another), Charlatan (a fraudulent claimant to skill), Fraud (a person who deceives for personal gain), Quack (a person who falsely claims medical skill) and Pretender (one who makes a false claim).

 

5 Important One-Word Substitutions

1. Autocrat (निरंकुश शासक): A ruler holding absolute, unchecked power

2. Demagogue (भड़काऊ लोकनेता): A leader who exploits popular prejudices for support

3. Anarchist (अराजकतावादी): One who believes all government should be abolished

4. Nihilist (शून्यवादी): One who rejects all religious and moral principles

5. Cynic (संशयवादी): One who believes people act only from self-interest
